question: On 23 September 2026, nine Sahrawi political prisoners of the Gdeim Izik group began an indefinite hunger strike in Moroccan prisons, after 16 years of detention.

According to Sahrawi and international human rights organisations, the prisoners are protesting against violations of their fundamental rights, including torture and ill treatment, prolonged solitary confinement, inadequate medical care and the refusal to transfer them to prisons closer to their families in Western Sahara.

They have also referred to findings and decisions of UN human rights mechanisms concerning their cases, including the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention and the Committee against Torture. In view of the potentially irreversible consequences of an indefinite hunger strike: 1.
What information does the Commission have regarding the current health and detention conditions of the prisoners, and has it raised their situation with Moroccan authorities?

Will the Commission raise this matter with the Member States and the relevant UN human rights mechanisms, and support coordinated EU diplomatic action to prevent irreversible harm and fundamental rights violations?
